title: "P²-Form" Strategic Management: Corporate Practices in Professional Partnerships
pub: Academy of Management Journal, Vol. 33, No. 4, pp. 725–755
author: Royston Greenwood · C. R. Hinings · John Brown

dom.t: Professional authority: AI enters an already contested field

mo.t: Professional authority: AI enters an already contested field

kp.k: Strategic management concerns center–business unit relationships
kp.d: The supplied abstract fragment frames strategic management in complex organizations around the relationship between the corporate center and principal business units. The fragment does not provide study findings or sufficient methodological detail to characterize the research further.
qs: Strategic management in complex organizations involves understanding the appropriate relationship between a corporate center and its principal business units.

kp.k: P²-Form links professional values with organizational arrangements
kp.d: The document's secondary-literature account describes P²-Form as an archetype connecting partnership, professionalism and peer control with structures and systems. The document explicitly warns that these characterizations were not read from the original paper and must not be attributed to Greenwood, Hinings and Brown as verified claims from it.
qs: These characterisations are how the later archetype literature describes the P²-Form.
The P²-Form archetype pairs an interpretive scheme (partnership, professionalism, peer control) with associated structures and systems.

kp.k: Partner governance disperses control and limits central command
kp.d: The secondary account identifies professional partners' combined ownership and control, collective and consensual governance, minimal hierarchy and dispersed strategic control as core structural features. In this characterization, the center coordinates rather than commands; this is a reported archetype description, not an independently supplied empirical finding.
qs: Core structural features: fusion of ownership and control in professional partners; collective and consensual governance; minimal hierarchy; strategic control dispersed to partners; a coordinating rather than commanding centre.

kp.k: Reported empirical setting is large accounting partnerships
kp.d: The secondary account says the empirical base is generally described as large accounting partnerships in the 1980s. No sample size, research design or detailed results are supplied. This is historical, cross-domain framework material, not evidence about AI or legal services.
qs: The empirical base is generally described as large accounting partnerships in the 1980s.

kp.k: Corporatization shifts partnerships toward managerial hierarchy and discipline
kp.d: The secondary account presents P²-Form as the baseline for subsequent research on professional-firm corporatization: movement toward managerial hierarchy, formal strategic planning and business-unit discipline, later theorized as the MPB archetype. The supplied document does not identify AI as a driver or report legal-profession outcomes.
qs: The archetype supplies the baseline from which subsequent research measured "corporatization" of professional firms — the drift toward managerial hierarchy, formal strategic planning, and business-unit discipline later theorized as the MPB archetype.
